faq: Why don't my marketing site and product share data?

They're on two subdomains, and the anonymous ID set on www is a different ID from the one set on app. Nothing links them. For the user it's one journey — see the ad, read the page, sign up, use the product. The data captures it as two disconnected halves.
What goes wrong when they're disconnected?

Marketing optimises to visitors, because that's the last thing it can see. Signups are cheap and most are worthless, so a channel can look excellent on cost per visitor while delivering users who never activate and never pay.
How do you stitch identity across subdomains?

Set your analytics identity cookie at the parent-domain level — .company.com rather than www.company.com — so it's readable on both. Then capture the acquisition context on the marketing site and carry it through: UTM parameters and click IDs, gclid from Google and fbclid from Meta.
Why is view-through attribution the worst offender?

A user scrolls past your ad, never clicks, arrives some other way and converts — and the platform counts it as its own. Both Google and Meta want credit for the same conversion, and both are graded by the companies selling you the clicks.
What table should you actually look at?

Rows are ad sources broken down as far as useful — channel, then campaign, then ad. Columns are the full journey: spend from the platform, through to activation and revenue from your product data. That last column flips decisions, and when it disagrees with the platform, the platform is wrong.
meta_description: Your marketing site and product live on two subdomains and never share data. How to stitch identity across them, and the weekly table it unlocks.
